description: Figure 4 illustrates the sparsity ratio before and after gating, displaying two lines representing different threshold values. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick labels at integer values. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at 0.2 intervals. The first line, colored blue and marked with circles, represents the “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03”, and begins at approximately 0.78 at Layer 0, decreases to 0.62 at Layer 5, and remains relatively stable around 0.60 to 0.65 from Layer 10 to Layer 20. The second line, colored orange and marked with squares, represents the “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.03”, and starts at approximately 0.76 at Layer 0, decreases to 0.60 at Layer 5, and remains relatively stable around 0.60 to 0.65 from Layer 10 to Layer 20. A third line, colored blue and marked with triangles, represents the “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.33”, and begins at approximately 0.68 at Layer 0, decreases to 0.55 at Layer 5, and remains relatively stable around 0.55 to 0.60 from Layer 10 to Layer 20. A fourth line, colored orange and marked with diamonds, represents the “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.33”, and starts at approximately 0.66 at Layer 0, decreases to 0.53 at Layer 5, and remains relatively stable around 0.53 to 0.58 from Layer 10 to Layer 20.
